settings.about.dataBody: Audio stays on this Mac. Transcripts, voice prints, settings and logs stay in your folders and the Keychain. Text goes only to the AI provider and Notion you set up, with your own keys. Nothing is sent to the author: no analytics, no tracking. Tell the people on your calls that you transcribe them and get consent where it is required.

keys.paste: Paste the key and press Return
set.pasteWithVAnd: Paste with ⌘V and press Return. Each key is checked with one request. Keys live only in the macOS Keychain and survive app updates.
set.claudeAccountClaudeCode: Claude account: Claude Code's own sign-in, uses your Claude plan. API key: the key in Keys, billed like the tips; use it when the plan's limit is reached.
set.sonnetReadsTheFiles: Sonnet reads the files and pulls out the facts well and fast; Opus is a little better on a hard call but slower and uses the plan's limit several times faster.
set.decidesIfATip: Decides if a tip is needed. Runs often: fast and cheap. Recommended: Haiku.
set.writesTheTipYou: Writes the tip you see. Recommended: Sonnet. Opus is too slow for live tips.
set.summaryAndAnalysisNot: Summary and analysis. Not time-critical. Recommended: Opus.
set.answerQuestionsToAnyone: Answer questions to anyone, not only to me
set.aQuestionAskedTo: A question asked to anyone on the call gets a tip when your brief, facts or the project's Current State hold an answer you could give or add. Off: only questions to you by name.
set.secondRequestWhenClaude: Second request when Claude is slow
set.ifClaudeShowsNo: If Claude shows no answer after 2 s (classify) or 3 s (tip), or fails at once, the same request is sent again and the first good answer wins. Faster tips on busy hours; costs a little more (both requests are billed and counted in the limits).
set.rateTipsAfterEach: Rate tips after each call (blind judge, about $0.10)
set.afterTheCallClaude: After the call Claude Sonnet scores up to 25 tips of the app and of the skill from the transcript, in the background. Results: <call>.judge/judge.summary.json next to the transcript.
set.atThisAmountIn: At this amount in one call the tips window shows a warning. Nothing stops.
set.atThisAmountClaude: At this amount Claude tips stop for the rest of the call. Local facts, cards and HELP NOW keep working.
set.atThisAmountClaude2: At this amount Claude tips stay off until the next month. The local layer keeps working.
set.theTipsWindowMenu: The tips window menu can switch it for one call only. Local models on this Mac: facts and cards by meaning, material for HELP NOW, project search. Off: keywords only.
set.builtInNothingElse: Built-in: nothing else to install. Ollama: your local Ollama server, shared with the Cowork skill.
set.anEmbeddingModelPulled: An embedding model pulled in Ollama. Another model needs a project reindex (lt index --rebuild) and its own thresholds.
set.builtInBgeM3: **Built-in.** bge-m3 by BAAI (open model, MIT license), a multilingual text embedding model: it turns a line of the call or a piece of a project file into numbers so that texts with the same meaning sit close, in Ukrainian, English and Spanish alike. Pacenote runs the int8 ONNX build (Xenova/bge-m3 on Hugging Face, about 570 MB) with ONNX Runtime on the CPU of this Mac: about 25 ms per line, about 1 s to start. The model lives in <app folder>/models/bge-m3-int8. Text never leaves the Mac.
set.ollamaIfYouAlready: **Ollama.** If you already run Ollama (ollama.com) for the Cowork skill, Pacenote can use the same server: `ollama pull bge-m3`, then choose Ollama here. Both engines give the same search results on the existing project index (checked: the same top result on 8 of 8 test queries), so switching needs no reindex.
set.anotherModelAnyEmbedding: **Another model.** Any embedding model from the Ollama library (for example multilingual-e5 or nomic-embed-text): `ollama pull <name>`, put the name into Model, then rebuild each project index with `lt index <project folder> --rebuild`. Thresholds in rules/semantic.yaml are tuned for bge-m3, so check them on a recorded call before trusting a new model. Other built-in models (any ONNX export with tokenizer.json) are planned; for now the built-in engine is bge-m3 only.
set.localAi: Instant search in your materials (on this Mac)
set.audioAndVoicePrints: Audio and voice prints never leave the Mac; only text goes to the Claude API.
set.tellsTheVoicesOn: Tells the voices on the other side apart (Speaker 2, Speaker 3) and asks "Who is speaking?" once a new voice talked for a few seconds. Names you give are used in tips and in the summary, and are remembered for the next calls.
set.nobodyYetNamesYou: Nobody yet. Names you give on calls appear here.
set.whichSideThisPerson: Which side this person is on: our team or the client's. Not during a call.
set.theCallsThisVoice: The calls this voice is suggested and recognised on: all projects, whole workspaces, or any number of projects (tick several). Not during a call.
set.removesThisPersonS: Removes this person's voice prints from the Mac. Not during a call.
set.inTheTipsWindow: In the tips window: the "Who is speaking?" card (pick a name from the project's people, type one, or Skip) and the speaker chip under the top bar to rename, fix one line or merge two voices. A voice named on a meeting series is named by itself on the next call of that series when it matches well (Clear speakers in the window forgets it). Each person has a side (Team, ours, or Client) and the calls they are suggested on: all projects, whole workspaces or several projects. The team table of a project config is Team on all projects; anyone else starts as Client of the call's project, and a person heard on another project's call gets that project added. Nothing is saved on a call marked Public in Start call. Voice prints stay in <app folder>/voices on this Mac.
set.addsTheProjectFolders: Adds the project folders of your workspaces. Folders that only look like workspaces are listed below to add or ignore; nothing else is added by itself.
set.rebuildTheSearchIndex: Rebuild the search index of every project with Index on (in the background, paused during calls).
set.setTheWorkFolder: Set the work folder in General first.
set.aWorkspaceSSubfolders: A workspace's subfolders become its projects. Ignore keeps a folder out of every scan.
set.noProjectsYetScan: No projects yet: Scan work folder.
set.noProjectsYetScan2: No projects yet. Scan the work folder, or add a project folder. Any folder works; Notion is not needed.
set.eachProjectIsA: Each project is a folder on your Mac: work folder > workspace > project. Calls, preparations and notes are saved in the project folder.
set.tickAProjectTo: Tick a project to see it in Start call. Untick a project that is over; nothing is deleted.
set.removesAProjectOr: ⋯ removes a project or a whole workspace from Pacenote. The folders stay on your Mac; Scan work folder or Add brings them back.
set.optionalExtrasComeFrom: Optional extras come from PM Control Tower (a separate free framework): a project file projects/<project>.md with the team, the Notion pages and the Meetings database. You get it when you set a project up there; then Add > Import Control Tower configs. Without it everything still works from the folders.
set.showInFinderRemove: Show in Finder, remove from Pacenote
set.activeOfferedInStart: Active: offered in Start call. Untick a project that is over; its folder and calls stay.
set.peopleNotionPagesAnd: People, Notion pages and settings come from
set.writeAMeetingPage: Write a meeting page after each call
set.afterTheCallA: After the call: a short summary, decisions, action items, open questions and the transcript, in the call's language. Missed one? Pacenote menu > Send last call to Notion.
set.projectsSetUpWith: Projects set up with PM Control Tower
set.theseProjectsHaveA: These projects have a PM Control Tower project file (projects/<project>.md) that names their Meetings database, so their pages go there. Every other project uses the database above. Without PM Control Tower this list is empty and nothing here applies.
set.runByYourOwn: Run by your own schedule (notion-mirror in Tools). Pacenote only reads it.
set.pacenoteRunsItEvery: Pacenote runs it every 2 hours (7:00-22:00), never during a call.
set.aReadOnlyCopy: A read-only copy of your Notion as .md files, refreshed by a background job every 2 hours. Pacenote reads it for facts and search; anything newer comes from the Notion API.
set.aReadOnlyCopy2: A read-only copy of your PM Control Tower Notion as files, for facts and search during calls. Needed only with PM Control Tower.
set.everyFormPeopleUse: Every form people use when they address you. When the other side says it with a question, you get a red "your turn" tip.
set.hideTheTipsWindow: Hide the tips window from screen sharing and screenshots
set.defaultForNewCalls: Default for new calls. The tips window menu changes it for one call only.
set.showThisWeekS: Show this week's numbers on Home
set.callsTimeOnCalls: Calls, time on calls, Claude spend, the chart and the monthly spend. Turn off to show Home to colleagues without your numbers.
set.settingsSaveAutomaticallyAnd: Settings save automatically and survive updates: options in Application Support/LiveTips, keys in the Keychain.
set.yourCorrectionsCardsOn: Your corrections (cards, On me, preparations, titles) are logged in edits.jsonl; each new preparation learns from them.
set.whenARecordingStarts: When a recording starts, macOS speaks the message through your speakers, so the others hear it through your microphone.
set.copyAConsentMessage: Copy a consent message for the meeting chat
set.whenARecordingStarts2: When a recording starts, the message is copied and a notification reminds you to paste it into the chat (Command-V).
set.offByDefaultThe: Off by default. The message follows the call's language. Check the rules of your company and your clients' countries: in some places everyone must agree to a recording.
set.theyWorkFromAny: They work from any app during a call, also while the meeting app has the focus. Change: press the new keys with Control, Option or Command (Esc cancels). Pause stops the transcript and the tips for both sides.
set.whereTheAppKeeps: Where the app keeps its recorder core, local AI model, state and logs. Default: <work folder>/Tools/LiveTips. When it changes, the files move there by themselves (not during a call).
cal.addEachGoogleOr: Add each Google or Microsoft account once in macOS; several of each are fine.
cal.googleAddAccountGoogle: Google: Add Account > Google, sign in, keep Calendars on. Microsoft 365 or Outlook: Add Account > Microsoft Exchange (work) or Outlook.com (personal).
cal.noCalendarsYetAdd: No calendars yet. Add an account above, wait a minute for the first sync, then Refresh.
cal.onlyTheTickedCalendars: Only the ticked calendars show in Home and Start call. Untick holidays, birthdays and calendars of other people.
cal.theReminderIsOff: The reminder is off by default: your calendar already reminds you. A regular call starts from the settings and the context of its last call (project, audience, type, languages, what matters, folders), so you only correct them.
cal.onlyTheTickedOnes: Only the ticked ones show in Home and Start call.

how.2: speech to text on the Mac
how.6: keyword rules, prepared facts and cards; Local AI matches them by meaning
how.8: classifies new lines, writes tips, answers asks and HELP NOW, searches the project folder
how.10: facts, tips, answers, transcript; nothing is sent to anyone
how.12: Your microphone and the call's system audio. Audio never leaves the Mac; the text transcript is written to the project's live folder.
how.14: Whisper (large-v3-turbo) runs on the Mac in the languages chosen in Start call. Ukrainian only is the default; add English when the call mixes languages.
how.16: A small voice model on the Mac tells voices apart. You name a voice once in the window; the name is remembered for the next calls of the same meeting series (project + title) and filled in by itself when the voice matches well. "Clear speakers" in the window forgets them.
how.18: bge-m3, an embedding model on the Mac, not a chat model. It finds prepared facts and cards by meaning, builds the search index of each project folder (updated after files change, paused during calls) and helps HELP NOW. It never writes tips by itself.
how.20: Only for projects with Claude tips on: the Cowork preparation (brief, facts, cards, outline), the call context you typed, the project's Current State from the Notion mirror, passages from the project folder found for that context, a digest of recent calls, and the last minutes of the transcript with speaker names. This context is cached for an hour, so each tip costs little.
how.22: A direct question or request to you, a date, an owner or a number goes straight to a tip; other new lines are checked by a fast model (Haiku) and turned into a tip only when they need one. Your asks in the window, HELP NOW and the folder search always go to Claude.
how.24: Every ~10 s a fast model (Haiku) updates the picture of the call: the topic and whose it is, open questions and requests to you, what you took on, decisions, and which speech points you said. The window shows it as the status line, the On me panel and the speech card; an open question to you that no tip covered gets one red tip.
how.26: The folder button: Claude turns your question into a few searches, reads the best passages from the project's files (by meaning with Local AI on, by words otherwise) and answers with the file names, in 10-30 s.
how.28: A wrap-up goes to the meeting's page in Notion (when the Notion token is set) and a quality check of the tips runs in the background.
how.30: The call and monthly budgets in Settings > AI stop Claude when reached; the Mac part keeps working.
how.32: Instant prepared facts; a tip within seconds after a direct question; answers to what you type; the transcript and speaker names saved in the project folder; nothing sent to the client or posted anywhere by itself.
how.34: Names, numbers and terms heard right every time (check them); similar voices always told apart; short replies tagged; Claude seeing your screen, chats or files outside the project folder; information newer than the last Notion mirror or index update; numbers Claude was not given. A project with Claude off gets only the Mac part.

prep.err.limit: The Claude account hit its limit: switch to API key and try again
tw.removeInfo: Its preparation files stay in the project's live folder.
tw.onTopOn: Always on top: on (click to let other windows cover it)
tw.onTopOff: Always on top: off (click to keep the window above other windows)
tw.startNowTip: Start recording now (otherwise it starts when the other side speaks)
tw.endInfo: Recording stops; the transcript and tips stay in the project folder, and the summary goes to Notion.
tw.closeOpen: Close this window and open Start call
tw.endedNoFile: Call ended, transcript file not found
tw.demoA: On a real call the answer appears here.
prep.err.noKey: No Claude API key in Settings > Keys
auto.title: Start tips for {title}?
auto.body: Project: {project}. Nothing is recorded until you start.
auto.chooseProject: Choose the project, then start. Nothing is recorded until you start.
auto.setting: Suggest starting tips when a call begins
auto.settingHelp: When Zoom, Microsoft Teams or a browser call (Google Meet) is on and the calendar has a call now, Pacenote offers to start tips once. It never records by itself.
callSettings.language.help: One or several languages of this call; the first ticked is the main one. Applies from the next line.
call.page.empty: Nothing was recorded for this call yet: no call picture or agenda.
followup.failed: The draft could not be written: {err}
followup.note: A draft in the client's language. Nothing is sent: edit it, then copy it or open it in Mail.
followup.subject: Subject
followup.title: Follow-up email: {title}
home.recent.help.page: Click: the call page. Right-click: Notion, the transcript, the follow-up email.
memory.help: Ask about the past calls of one project (Command-F).
memory.notFound: Nothing about this in the calls of this project.
memory.note: Only the transcripts of the chosen project are searched. The question and the passages found go to Claude.
memory.prompt: What did we agree about the export?
memory.title: Call memory
py.failed: No answer from the tips engine; see logs/after-call.log
py.noEngine: The tips engine is not installed: Settings > About > Install or repair
rehearse.failed: The rehearsal step did not work: {err}
rehearse.noSteps: This preparation has no outline or slides. You can still practise the questions.
rehearse.note: A rehearsal: nothing is recorded and nothing is written to the project.
rehearse.title: Rehearsal: {title}
risk.add.help: Writes one page into the project's Notion risk database, after you confirm.
risk.confirm.body: “{risk}” goes into the risk database of {project} in Notion.
risk.confirm.title: Add this risk to the risk register?
risk.noDB: The project config has no risk database (risks_db).
series.title: Series: {title}
stats.prepVsNot: Decisions per call: {a} with a brief, {b} without.
stats.talkShare.sub: share of the words, on average
stats.unanswered.sub: to you, at the end of the calls
transcript.title: Transcript: {title}
ai.access.accountHelp: Your Claude plan through Claude Code: no key, the work counts against the plan's limits.
ai.access.footer: Set once for the whole app. Each job below picks which of the two it uses.
ai.tips.codeWhy: Not recommended for tips: each request through Claude Code starts a few seconds later than through the key, without prompt caching or a second request when Claude is slow, and an hour of a call is hundreds of requests from your plan's limits. A tip that comes late is no use. Good as a backup when the API credit runs out.
ai.after.footer: Summary and Notion page, follow-up email, call memory, rehearsal and the tip judge. Not time-critical, so your Claude account is a good fit.
ai.auto: Switch automatically when one way is out
ai.auto.help: When the chosen way stops working (the API credit is used up, the plan limit is reached, you are signed out), the job uses the other one. The chosen way is checked again before the next job (during a call every 2 minutes), and the job goes back to it as soon as it answers.
ai.status.out: {route}: {reason} since {time}. Jobs that use it go the other way until it answers again.
ai.reason.auth: signed out or the key is not valid
prep.switched: Switched to {route}: the chosen way is out
start.regularHint: Tips follow the agenda, open questions and what is on you. Pick Presentation to attach a deck.
deck.title: Presentation
deck.formats: PDF, PowerPoint, Keynote or a text outline. You can also drop the file here.
deck.promise: Prepare reads the deck, writes your talk slide by slide, times each slide and the questions the audience may ask.
deck.readingHint: Keep filling the form. Slide owners and timing unlock when reading is done.
deck.err.title: Can't read {file}
deck.err.keynote: Keynote isn't installed on this Mac, so the slides can't be opened. Export the deck as PDF and attach it.
deck.ownersHint: Click a slide to change, or assign a range
deck.allHint: "All" means a shared slide: tips show, nobody gets a handoff card. On {name}'s slides the tips window stays quiet and tells you when your turn comes.
deck.talkTime: Talk time is {t}: {d} call minus {q} Q&A. Prepare times the slides to fit it.
talk.title: Your talk, slide by slide
talk.colleague: {name} presents. No talk written for these slides, no tips during them. You get a "your turn" card before slide {n}.
talk.saveHint: Edits save as you type. The tips window and rehearsal use this text.
again.title: Prepare again?
again.age: Brief is {d} days old · {n} changes since
again.keepHint: Slides you edited ({list}) stay as they are. The rest is rewritten.
again.rewriteHint: Your edits on {n} slides are replaced. You can restore them after.
again.workingHint: Your edits on slides {list} stay. While updating, these slides can be read, not edited.
again.done: Talk updated · {n} slides rewritten, {k} kept with your edits
pm.adv.skip: Skip slide {n} to catch up. It is marked as can skip.
pm.adv.shorten: Shorten slide {n} to one sentence to catch up.
pm.nextColleague: After this slide {name} presents {range}. Tips go quiet until slide {n}.
pm.syncB.label: Slides follow your speech · asks before moving
pm.colleagueHint: Tips stay quiet while {name} speaks. Questions to you still get an answer card.
pm.empty.title: No presentation attached
pm.empty.text: Attach a file and Pacenote shows the slides, the time for each and answers to questions. Until then, tips work as on a regular call.
reh.title: Rehearse your talk
reh.meta: About {t}. Nothing is recorded: no audio, no transcript.
reh.step1: Run through your slides out loud.
reh.step1Hint: Each slide has a timer. Press Next when you finish. You present {n} slides, {name}'s are skipped.
reh.step2Hint: Claude plays the client, {name}, and asks what this audience is likely to ask.
reh.step3Hint: Short is fine. You get a score for each and a better first sentence.
reh.step4Hint: Overall score, timing per slide and what to change in the talk.
reh.stopAny: You can stop at any step
reh.outLoud: Say it out loud. Pacenote only counts the time on each slide.
reh.answerHint: Keep it short, as you would say it. Scores come after all 4 questions.
reh.applyHint: Apply to talk shortens slides {list} and adds the better answers to their Q&A. You review it in Your talk before it is saved.
after.series: Part of a series: {name}, call {n}. Calls in this project with the same title are linked. Open items and agenda points not raised go into the next brief, {next}.
after.neverSends: Pacenote never sends it for you
series.whyText: Same project and the same call title. Pacenote links such calls: open promises and agenda points not raised go into the next brief. To start a new series, rename the call.
sys.noAudioWhy: No sound from the microphone or the call for 30 s. Usually another app took the microphone, or macOS revoked access after an update.
sys.noAudioFoot: Tips are off until audio comes back. What was said before {t} is saved.
sys.noOtherTitle: No call audio is coming in
sys.noOtherWhy: Your microphone works, but there is no system audio from the call for 30 s. If the call is in a browser and you can hear it, switch the sound output to another device and back: the browser reconnects its audio. Otherwise the call plays through another device, or Pacenote lost access to system audio.
sys.noOtherFoot: Your words are recorded. Tips about the other side are off until their audio comes back.
deck.err.generic: The file can't be opened or has no slides. Export the deck as PDF and attach it, or paste the talk as text.
deck.pasteHint: One slide per block: start each with "# Title" or "Slide 3:", or leave a blank line between slides.
talk.adv: Shorten slide {n} or mark slide {m} as can skip.
talk.short: If short on time, say only
talk.proposal: From the rehearsal: slides {list} shortened, {k} better answers added. Review them below, then save.
after.instruct: What to change: "drop the pricing line", "shorter"
set.mergeHelp: The same person under another name: {name}'s voice prints join the chosen person, and {name} becomes another spelling of that name (typing or picking it names the kept person).
again.keepBrief: The brief is written again from the newest sources. The current one is kept as the previous version.
setup.step.claude.title: Claude Code
setup.step.claude.why: Prepares your calls (brief, cards, facts). Needed whichever way you pay: your Claude plan or an API key. Recording works without it.
onboarding.unsigned.title: Why macOS asked you to press Open Anyway
onboarding.unsigned.body: This beta is signed by its developer but not notarized by Apple yet, so macOS asks once before the first launch. The app is not changed; Apple just has not reviewed it. A new version you download may ask again: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway.
sign.title: Signature
sign.developer: Signed by the developer, not notarized by Apple (beta). macOS asks for Open Anyway on the first launch of each downloaded version.
start.transcriptHint: Records the call and writes the transcript, no tips during the call. After it: the summary, the meeting page and the follow-up as usual. No preparation needed.
callSettings.tips.hint: Off: only the transcript; the summary and the follow-up after the call as usual
ai.local.hint: A preparation on this Mac: the app gathers the files and the model writes the brief. Free, slower, simpler than Claude.
ai.local.noOllama: Ollama does not answer. Open the Ollama app (or run: ollama serve).
ai.local.ready: Ollama is running and has this model.
ai.local.notPulled: Ollama is running, the model is not downloaded yet: {cmd}
local.footer: Free and private, slower and simpler than Claude. Used where a job's "Runs on" is On this Mac (preparation, after the call); not for tips during a call (too slow, and the call needs the memory).
local.notRunning: Ollama is installed but not running.
local.noModels: Ollama is running, no model yet.
local.pull.done: Installed. It is in the model lists now.
local.model.search: {name}: search in documents (Local AI), cannot write text
search.textModel: {name} is also on this Mac: it writes text (preparation, after the call), but cannot search (Ollama makes no search vectors for it).
search.what: During a call, every line is matched against your facts, cards and project documents in about a second, so the right fact shows up without waiting for Claude. bge-m3 is a search model: it finds, it does not write.
local.fallback: Use it when Claude does not answer
local.fallback.help: When neither the Claude account nor the API key can run, the preparation and the after-the-call jobs run on this model. Tips during a call stay on Claude.
ntask.removed: Removed, and moved to the Notion trash
ntask.removeRefused: Removed here; the page stayed in Notion (no access to change it)
ntask.mapNotice: Map {project} to send its tasks to Notion
ntask.removeHelp: Remove from On you and move the Notion page to the trash
ntask.trashInfo: Pacenote did not make this task. Notion keeps it in the trash for 30 days.
ntset.footer: Your Notion tasks join On you on Home and the On me tab of the call window. Nothing is written to Notion unless you tick, remove or add a task, or turn on the switch below.
ntset.enable: Show my Notion tasks in On you
ntset.tickSets: When I check a task, set
ntset.autoAdd: Add my commitments from each call to Notion tasks
comp.for.ollama: Runs a model on this Mac (plan B for the preparation and the after-call work).
comp.for.model: Preparation and after-call work without Claude.
comp.for.link: Transcribing a link: Google Drive, YouTube, Vimeo.
comp.addonsFoot: Install only what you need. None of them is needed to record calls.
comp.onb.title: Optional add-ons
comp.onb.body: You can add these now or later in Settings. Nothing is needed to record a call.
comp.onb.space: About 16 GB of disk; {free} GB free now.
tr.subtitle: A file or a link becomes a transcript like a call: the same speech model and voices.
tr.drop: Drop an audio or video file here
tr.types: mp3, m4a, wav, aac, flac, ogg, mp4, mov, m4v, webm, mkv; up to 4 hours
tr.privacy: Transcribed on this Mac. Nothing leaves it until you click Add to Notion.
tr.background: You can close this window: a notification says when it is done.
tr.needsLinkDl: Transcribing a link needs the Link downloader (Settings > General > Optional add-ons).
tr.downloadFailed: The link could not be downloaded.
tr.cannotRead: This file cannot be read as audio. Try another format (mp3, m4a, wav, mp4).
tr.tooLong: The recording is longer than 4 hours.
tr.title: Title
tr.nothingSent: Nothing is sent without a click.
tr.noMeetingsDb: Choose where meeting pages go in Settings > Notion first.
tr.addedToProject: Added to the project's live folder; the next preparation reads it.
comp.startToUse: downloaded; start Ollama to use it
ntset.enable.i: Your open Notion tasks appear in On you on Home and in the call window's On me, next to the commitments from calls.
ntset.database.i: The Notion database with your tasks. It must be shared with the Pacenote integration (••• > Connections in Notion).
ntset.onMeMeans.i: Which person property marks a task as yours (Assignee, Owner) and which person you are. Only tasks with you there are shown.
ntset.showOnlyWhen.i: Only tasks with one of the highlighted values are shown. Click a value to add or remove it. Several conditions must all hold.
ntset.tickSets.i: What a check mark in Pacenote writes to Notion, for example Status = Done. Undo puts the old value back.
ntset.due.i: The date property used for the due date and for sorting (overdue first).
ntset.period.i: Only tasks changed in Notion during this period are shown. All shows every open task.
ntset.autoAdd.i: After each call, the commitments on you from that call become tasks in this database, with Undo. Commitments of other people never go to Notion.
ntset.pickProperty: Choose a property, then click the values to keep.
ntset.projectBy.i: The property that tells which project a task belongs to (a relation to your projects, or a select). Pacenote matches the names; set the rest below.
ntset.projectsFooter: Which Notion project each Pacenote project is. One Pacenote project can have several Notion values. A call shows the tasks of its project; a workspace call shows all its projects.
ntset.workspaceRel.i: Tasks whose {prop} is this value are added to the workspace's calls.
